differences.what: massing: the draft's hipped block is now the photograph's house, two storeys of brick over a high basement under a dormered mansard, filling about the same part of the frame (the photograph's house x 190-850 px of the side-by-side's left half, the render's about x 240-845)

the front's composition from the north: a canted bay with two lights a storey, the door's column over a straight stoop, then the corner block's two lights a storey, round-headed in the principal storey
a dormer over each column of the front and on the 20th Street face, and the canted south-west corner with the flank's bay behind it

the corner block's mansard stands about a storey higher than the rest in the photograph (its dormers' heads at y 230-330 px against the north bay's at y 330-400); the build carries the whole mansard at one height
the north bay rises under its own curved mansard with two dormers in the photograph; the build stops it under the cornice with a low hip and the house's mansard behind

the door stands under a round arch in the photograph (its ring x 462-535 px, its crown about y 695, level with the corner block's round heads); T-3283 cuts it round-headed in the brick, 1.3 m across and 3.4 m to the crown, a pair of leaves under a fanlight in a deep reveal, under the round lights' own arch band and key, and the render's crown stands within a few px of the photograph's

the camera sees the 20th Street flank more openly than the render (the flank's bay at x 1050-1200 px of the box); the eye is held at a chosen stand (26.6 px RMS) and the flank's depth of view is not fitted; and the front's north half is drawn narrower than the photograph's: the north bay's lights and the door both stand about 55-60 px south of the photograph's while the corner block's lights land on theirs, so the door's column agrees with the picture relative to the bay and the gap is the camera's, not the door's (T-3283)
the chamber storey's corner lights read slightly arched in the halftone; the build's are flat-headed
the walls are under a heavy creeper in 1928; its 1904 extent is not known, and the build shows the brick bare
colour: a monochrome halftone, and the walls are under creeper

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance | owner ruling} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153); owner ruling where the owner asked the build to depart from the picture (T-3236).
